definitions.explanation: Paper manufactured using Western methods, as opposed to traditional Japanese washi. The standard paper used for printing, writing, and everyday purposes.

examples.japanese: {洋紙|ようし}と{和紙|わし}の{違|ちが}い。
examples.english: The difference between Western paper and washi.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}に{洋紙|ようし}の{製造|せいぞう}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: Western-style paper manufacturing began in the Meiji period.

examples.japanese: {現在|げんざい}の{日本|にほん}で{使|つか}われている{紙|かみ}のほとんどは{洋紙|ようし}だ。
examples.english: Most of the paper used in modern Japan is Western-style paper.

notes:
{洋紙|ようし} is the technical term for Western-style machine-made paper, as opposed to traditional Japanese {和紙|わし}.

FORMS:
{洋|よう} (Western) + {紙|し} (paper)

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, people simply say {紙|かみ} since Western paper is the default. {洋紙|ようし} is mainly used when specifically contrasting with {和紙|わし}, or in technical and industrial contexts.
Do not confuse with the homophone {用紙|ようし} (paper/form for a specific purpose), which is far more common in daily life.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {和紙|わし}: Japanese paper — traditional handmade paper from plant fibers like {楮|こうぞ}
- {紙|かみ}: paper — the general everyday word
- {用紙|ようし}: a form or sheet of paper (different kanji, same reading)
